claim: Mammalian CpG islands (CGIs) differ sharply from the bulk genome by being rich in G + C.
source: The mammalian genome is punctuated by CpG islands (CGIs), which differ sharply from the bulk genome by being rich in G + C and the dinucleotide CpG.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of CGIs.

claim: Mammalian CpG islands (CGIs) differ sharply from the bulk genome by being rich in the dinucleotide CpG.
source: The mammalian genome is punctuated by CpG islands (CGIs), which differ sharply from the bulk genome by being rich in G + C and the dinucleotide CpG.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of CGIs.

claim: CGIs often include transcription initiation sites.
source: CGIs often include transcription initiation sites and display 'active' histone marks, notably histone H3 lysine 4 methylation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known feature of CGIs.

claim: CGIs display 'active' histone marks, notably histone H3 lysine 4 methylation.
source: CGIs often include transcription initiation sites and display 'active' histone marks, notably histone H3 lysine 4 methylation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known feature of CGIs.

claim: In embryonic stem cells (ESCs) some CGIs adopt a 'bivalent' chromatin state bearing simultaneous 'active' and 'inactive' chromatin marks.
source: In embryonic stem cells (ESCs) some CGIs adopt a 'bivalent' chromatin state bearing simultaneous 'active' and 'inactive' chromatin marks.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known feature of CGIs in ESCs.

claim: Bivalency is the default chromatin structure for CpG-rich, G + C-rich DNA.
source: We found that bivalency is the default chromatin structure for CpG-rich, G + C-rich DNA.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on the experimental results with artificial CGIs.

claim: A high CpG density alone is not sufficient for bivalent chromatin formation, as A + T-rich sequence settings invariably provoke de novo DNA methylation leading to loss of CGI signature chromatin.
source: A high CpG density alone is not sufficient for this effect, as A + T-rich sequence settings invariably provoke de novo DNA methylation leading to loss of CGI signature chromatin.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental results with A+T-rich, CpG-rich sequences.

claim: Both CpG-richness and G + C-richness are required for induction of signature chromatin structures at CGIs.
source: We conclude that both CpG-richness and G + C-richness are required for induction of signature chromatin structures at CGIs.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: CpG islands mark most gene promoters.
source: CpG islands (CGIs) are stretches of atypical genomic DNA sequences that mark most gene promoters (Bird, 1986; Deaton and Bird, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Mammalian CGIs have a G + C-rich base composition of 65% versus 40% for the bulk genome.
source: Though individually unique in nucleotide sequence, mammalian CGIs share two features that often correlate but can vary independently: a G + C-rich base composition (65% vs 40% for the bulk genome) and high density of the dinucleotide CpG (5–10-fold higher than the bulk genome).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a known characteristic of CGIs.

claim: Mammalian CGIs have a CpG density 5–10-fold higher than the bulk genome.
source: Though individually unique in nucleotide sequence, mammalian CGIs share two features that often correlate but can vary independently: a G + C-rich base composition (65% vs 40% for the bulk genome) and high density of the dinucleotide CpG (5–10-fold higher than the bulk genome).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a known characteristic of CGIs.

claim: Bulk genomic DNA is globally methylated, whereas CGIs associated with promoters invariably lack DNA methylation.
source: Whereas bulk genomic DNA is globally methylated, CGIs associated with promoters invariably lack DNA methylation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a known feature distinguishing CGIs from bulk DNA.

claim: CGIs function as generic platforms for gene regulation, probably via proteins that bind to CpG and influence chromatin modification.
source: It has been proposed that CGIs function as generic platforms for gene regulation, probably via proteins that bind to CpG and influence chromatin modification (Blackledge and Klose, 2011; Deaton and Bird, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Enrichment or depletion of specific chromatin marks at CGIs is linked to proteins that bind to unmethylated CpG.
source: This hypothesis has gained credence due to accumulating evidence that enrichment or depletion of specific chromatin marks at CGIs is linked to proteins that bind to unmethylated CpG.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as supporting evidence for the CGI function hypothesis.

claim: All proteins that bind to unmethylated CpG possess CXXC zinc finger domains that bind specifically to the CpG dyad in duplex DNA.
source: So far, all such proteins possess CXXC zinc finger domains that bind specifically to the CpG dyad in duplex DNA (Lee et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Cfp1 is a CXXC domain-containing component of the Set1/COMPASS complex.
source: Cfp1, for example, is a CXXC domain-containing component of the Set1/COMPASS complex (Lee and Skalnik, 2005), which generates H3K4 methylation, a signature chromatin mark at non-methylated CGIs (Bernstein et al., 2006; Guenther et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The Set1/COMPASS complex generates H3K4 methylation, a signature chromatin mark at non-methylated CGIs.
source: Cfp1, for example, is a CXXC domain-containing component of the Set1/COMPASS complex (Lee and Skalnik, 2005), which generates H3K4 methylation, a signature chromatin mark at non-methylated CGIs (Bernstein et al., 2006; Guenther et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Cfp1 is concentrated at CGIs as determined by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP).
source: Accordingly, Cfp1 is concentrated at CGIs as determined by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and its absence is associated with reduced H3K4 methylation at many CGIs (Thomson et al., 2010; Clouaire et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Absence of Cfp1 is associated with reduced H3K4 methylation at many CGIs.
source: Accordingly, Cfp1 is concentrated at CGIs as determined by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and its absence is associated with reduced H3K4 methylation at many CGIs (Thomson et al., 2010; Clouaire et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The H3K4 methyltransferases Mll1 and Mll2 are CXXC proteins found at CGIs in mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: The H3K4 methyltransferases Mll1 and Mll2 are also CXXC proteins and each is found at CGIs in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) as determined by ChIP-Seq (Hu et al., 2013; Denissov et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The CXXC domain-containing proteins Kdm2a and Kdm2b are enriched at CGIs.
source: Similarly the CXXC domain-containing proteins Kdm2a and Kdm2b are enriched at CGIs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a known feature of these proteins.

claim: Kdm2a is an H3K36 demethylase that contributes to depletion of H3K36me at CGI promoters.
source: Kdm2a is an H3K36 demethylase that contributes to depletion of H3K36me at CGI promoters (Blackledge et al., 2010), whereas Kdm2b facilitates recruitment of the PRC1 complex to transcriptionally silent CGIs (Farcas et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Kdm2b facilitates recruitment of the PRC1 complex to transcriptionally silent CGIs.
source: Kdm2a is an H3K36 demethylase that contributes to depletion of H3K36me at CGI promoters (Blackledge et al., 2010), whereas Kdm2b facilitates recruitment of the PRC1 complex to transcriptionally silent CGIs (Farcas et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Promoter-less CGI-like DNA sequences of invertebrate origin in mouse ES cells cause local enrichment of trimethylation of lysine 4 of histone H3 (H3K4me3).
source: Promoter-less CGI-like DNA sequences of invertebrate origin in mouse ES cells were initially shown to cause local enrichment of trimethylation of lysine 4 of histone H3 (H3K4me3) and to recruit the CpG binding protein Cfp1 (Thomson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Promoter-less CGI-like DNA sequences of invertebrate origin in mouse ES cells recruit the CpG binding protein Cfp1.
source: Promoter-less CGI-like DNA sequences of invertebrate origin in mouse ES cells were initially shown to cause local enrichment of trimethylation of lysine 4 of histone H3 (H3K4me3) and to recruit the CpG binding protein Cfp1 (Thomson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: G + C-rich DNA derived from bacteria creates chromatin marked by both H3K27me3 and H3K4me3.
source: Similar experiments using G + C-rich DNA derived from bacteria created chromatin marked by both H3K27me3 and H3K4me3 (Mendenhall et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: H3K4me3 is characteristic of active promoters.
source: Whereas H3K4me3 is characteristic of active promoters, H3K27me3 is associated with transcriptional repression via the polycomb complex.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: H3K27me3 is associated with transcriptional repression via the polycomb complex.
source: Whereas H3K4me3 is characteristic of active promoters, H3K27me3 is associated with transcriptional repression via the polycomb complex.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The coincidence of H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 in 'bivalent' chromatin is thought to be a feature of genes that are poised to become either active or silent during early development.
source: The coincidence of these two marks in so-called 'bivalent' chromatin is thought to be a feature of genes that are poised to become either active or silent during early development (Azuara et al., 2006; Bernstein et al., 2006; Voigt et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Many native CGIs in ESCs adopt a 'bivalent' chromatin structure when transcriptionally silent.
source: Many native CGIs in ESCs adopt a 'bivalent' chromatin structure when transcriptionally silent.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Artificial CGI 1 has a CpG frequency of one per ∼10 base pairs and a base composition of 65% G + C.
source: A computer-generated CGI-like sequence (Artificial CGI 1) was designed with a CpG frequency of one per ∼10 base pairs and a base composition of 65% G + C (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This describes the design of the experimental construct.

claim: The CGI-like insertions consistently generated a bivalent chromatin structure marked by H3K4me3 and H3K27me3.
source: The CGI-like insertions consistently generated a bivalent chromatin structure marked by H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 (Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by ChIP data shown in the figures.

claim: The levels of H3K4me3 at the artificial CGI were similar to those at the endogenous bivalent gene Hoxc8.
source: The levels of H3K4me3 at the artificial CGI were similar to those at the endogenous bivalent gene Hoxc8, whereas H3K4me3 levels in the DNA sequences flanking the CGI were unaffected by the insertion.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the ChIP data.

claim: H3K4me3 levels in the DNA sequences flanking the artificial CGI were unaffected by the insertion.
source: The levels of H3K4me3 at the artificial CGI were similar to those at the endogenous bivalent gene Hoxc8, whereas H3K4me3 levels in the DNA sequences flanking the CGI were unaffected by the insertion.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the ChIP data.

claim: H3K27me3 spread variably into flanking regions of the human BAC.
source: H3K27me3 was less discrete, spreading variably into flanking regions of the human BAC, but Suz12, a component of the PRC2 complex that deposits the H3K27me3 mark, was tightly localised to the CGI-like sequence in each case.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the ChIP data.

claim: Suz12, a component of the PRC2 complex that deposits the H3K27me3 mark, was tightly localised to the CGI-like sequence.
source: H3K27me3 was less discrete, spreading variably into flanking regions of the human BAC, but Suz12, a component of the PRC2 complex that deposits the H3K27me3 mark, was tightly localised to the CGI-like sequence in each case.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the ChIP data.

claim: All the artificial CGI insertions reproducibly maintained a low level of DNA methylation.
source: The DNA methylation status of the integrated artificial CGIs was investigated by bisulfite sequencing. This showed that all the insertions reproducibly maintained a low level of DNA methylation (Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from bisulfite sequencing data.

claim: DNA methylation levels at CGI-like sequences inserted into the gene desert (∼10%) were consistently somewhat higher than in the cassette exchange system (0.5%).
source: DNA methylation levels at CGI-like sequences inserted into the gene desert (∼10%) were consistently somewhat higher than in the cassette exchange system (0.5%) and were somewhat higher than an endogenous control CGI in the same DNA samples (Dlx5; ∼4–5%, data not shown).
evidence: This is an experimental observation comparing methylation levels across different integration systems.

claim: None of the promoter-less artificial DNA sequences displayed a peak of RNA polymerase II over the insert.
source: To test whether these promoter-less artificial DNA sequences were transcriptionally inert, we performed ChIP with antibodies recognising three differentially phosphorylated forms of RNA polymerase II in replicate cell lines. None displayed a peak over the insert, whereas control active genes were RNA polymerase-positive as expected (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNA Pol II ChIP data.

claim: The artificial CGI-like insertions did not display significant peaks of histone acetylation.
source: Consistent with the absence of RNA polymerase, we did not detect significant peaks of histone acetylation over the CGI-like insertions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from histone acetylation ChIP data.

claim: Bivalent chromatin is the default state for transcriptionally inert CGI-like DNA in ESCs.
source: In summary, data derived from three distinct promoter-less CGI-like sequences indicate that bivalent chromatin is the default state for transcriptionally inert CGI-like DNA in ESCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on multiple artificial CGI constructs.

claim: Cfp1 is enriched at the CGI-like sequences.
source: We next asked whether the CXXC protein Cfp1 is enriched at the CGI-like sequences. To facilitate detection of Cfp1, we introduced the BAC containing the artificial CGI into a transgenic cell line expressing a Cfp1-GFP fusion protein (Denissov et al., 2014). Having verified that a bivalent domain was formed at the artificial CGI in these cells (data not shown), ChIP was performed on three independent cell lines using an anti-GFP antibody. We consistently observed discrete enrichment of Cfp1 at the CGI-like insertion (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from Cfp1-GFP ChIP data.

claim: Cfp1 is not required for the formation of H3K4me3 levels at the bivalent domain.
source: To determine whether the formation of a bivalent domain at the inserted artificial CGI-like sequence was dependent on Cfp1, the artificial CGI was introduced into Cfp1−/− mouse ES cells (Carlone and Skalnik, 2001) and three independent lines were analysed by ChIP. H3K4me3 levels at the artificial CGI were clearly detectable in the Cfp1−/− cells, indicating that Cfp1 is not required for the formation of H3K4me3 levels at the bivalent domain (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from ChIP data in Cfp1 knockout cells.

claim: Depletion of Cfp1 preferentially causes a decrease of H3K4me3 at active genes without affecting non-productive genes.
source: Depletion of Cfp1 was previously reported to preferentially cause a decrease of H3K4me3 at active genes without affecting non-productive genes (Clouaire et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Reduced H3K4me3 was observed at the active control gene Sox2 in Cfp1−/− cells compared to wildtype cells.
source: In agreement with this finding, we observed reduced H3K4me3 at the active control gene Sox2 compared to wildtype cells (Compare Figures 2D and 1C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from ChIP data comparing wildtype and Cfp1 knockout cells.

claim: During differentiation of ESCs to neuronal progenitor cells, there is a consistent drop in H3K4me3 accompanied by persistent or increased H3K27me3 at the artificial CGI.
source: We also followed the fate of chromatin modifications during differentiation of ESCs to neuronal progenitor cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and found a consistent drop in H3K4me3 accompanied by persistent or increased H3K27me3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from ChIP data during differentiation.

claim: The transition from bivalency to H3K27me3 marking alone at the artificial CGI matches that at native CGI-associated genes that remain transcriptionally silent during differentiation.
source: This transition from bivalency to H3K27me3 marking alone matches that at native CGI-associated genes that remain transcriptionally silent during differentiation (Bernstein et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental findings with published data.

claim: The Low CpG / High G + C sequence failed to create bivalent chromatin as neither H3K4me3 nor H3K27me3 was detected.
source: An artificial CGI with a base composition similar to that of a normal CGI (65% G + C) but with a low density of CpGs, similar to that of the bulk genome (1 CpG/100 bp), was designed (Low CpG / High G + C). This Low CpG / High G + C sequence failed to create bivalent chromatin as neither H3K4me3 nor H3K27me3 was detected in three independent ESC lines (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from ChIP data on the Low CpG / High G+C construct.

claim: A G + C-rich base composition alone is insufficient to recruit either H3K4me3 or H3K27me3.
source: Our conclusion from this data is that a G + C-rich base composition alone is insufficient to recruit either H3K4me3 or H3K27me3.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Low CpG / High G+C experimental data.

claim: None of the A + T-rich, CpG-rich insertions generated a focus of bivalent chromatin in multiple independent cell lines.
source: To test this idea, we generated four different artificial DNA sequences that were CpG-rich to the same level as typical CGIs (10 CpGs/100 bp), but relatively A + T-rich in overall base composition (three of 40% and one of 50% G + C on average; Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—source data 1). Contrary to expectation, none of these insertions generated a focus of bivalent chromatin in multiple independent cell lines (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from ChIP data on A+T-rich, CpG-rich constructs.

claim: All A + T-rich, CpG-rich CGI insertions had become densely methylated at CpGs in replicate cell lines.
source: A potential explanation for this finding came from an analysis of DNA methylation status, which showed that in replicate cell lines the CGIs had all become densely methylated at CpGs (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from bisulfite sequencing data.

claim: Base composition is a strong determinant of DNA methylation status.
source: The striking contrast between the consistent methylation-free status of three separate G + C-rich, CpG-rich integrants and the reproducible dense methylation of four unrelated A + T-rich, CpG-rich sequences of the same length indicates that base composition is a strong determinant of DNA methylation status.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing methylation patterns of different constructs.

claim: There is a sharp transition in CpG methylation between 50 and 60% G + C content.
source: A plot of G + C-content against percentage CpG methylation showed a sharp transition between 50 and 60% G + C (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an observation from plotting methylation data against G+C content.

claim: When the High CpG /High A + T construct was introduced into Dnmt 3a/3b knock out cells it remained unmethylated and bivalent chromatin was detected at the inserted sequence.
source: When the High CpG /High A + T construct was introduced into Dnmt 3a/3b knock out cells it now remained unmethylated, and importantly, bivalent chromatin was detected at the inserted sequence (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from ChIP and bisulfite sequencing in Dnmt3a/3b knockout cells.

claim: H3K4me3 was reproducibly weaker than controls in Dnmt 3a/Dnmt 3b double mutant cells, whereas a robust H3K27me3 signal was obtained.
source: We noticed that H3K4me3 was reproducibly weaker than controls in Dnmt 3a/Dnmt 3b double mutant cells, whereas a robust H3K27me3 signal was obtained.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from ChIP data in Dnmt3a/3b knockout cells.

claim: A + T-rich DNA is less able to recruit H3K4me3 despite its high CpG density.
source: This may indicate that A + T-rich DNA is less able to recruit H3K4me3 despite its high CpG density.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observation in Dnmt3a/3b knockout cells.

claim: Growing cells in 2i medium for 10 days reduced the average level of genomic CpG methylation from ∼95% to ∼55%.
source: The dominance of the polycomb-associated H3K27me3 mark at A + T-rich CGIs was also seen when DNA methylation was partially reduced by growing cells for 10 days in 2i medium, which enhances the pluripotent state. In line with previous reports (Ficz et al., 2013; Habibi et al., 2013), we found that the average level of genomic CpG methylation was reduced from ∼95% to ∼55% (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from bisulfite sequencing with supporting citations.

claim: Cells grown in 2i medium displayed a strong increase in H3K27me3 without the appearance of noticeable H3K4me3 at the A+T-rich, CpG-rich construct.
source: Whereas cells grown in serum-containing medium lacked both the tested histone marks, 2i-grown cells displayed a strong increase in H3K27me3 without the appearance of noticeable H3K4me3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from ChIP data comparing serum and 2i culture conditions.

claim: While CpG frequency is a key feature of CGIs that determines the signature chromatin marks at CGIs, A + T-richness confers an intrinsic susceptibility to de novo methylation that is dominant over these chromatin modifications.
source: We conclude that while CpG frequency is a key feature of CGIs that determines the signature chromatin marks at CGIs, A + T-richness confers an intrinsic susceptibility to de novo methylation that is dominant over these chromatin modifications (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings on A+T-rich constructs.

claim: 1954 G + C-rich (≥61%), CpG deficient (≤1/100 bp) sequences of ≥500 bp in length were identified in the mouse genome.
source: We searched first for G + C-rich (≥61%), CpG deficient (≤1/100 bp) sequences of ≥500 bp in length and identified 1954 examples.
evidence: This is a result from computational analysis of the mouse genome.

claim: None of the G + C-rich, CpG deficient sequences coincided with bivalent chromatin in ESCs.
source: None of these coincided with bivalent chromatin in ESCs, in agreement with our results using synthetic DNA.
evidence: This is a result from comparing genomic sequences with published chromatin data.

claim: Uniformly A + T-rich and CpG-rich DNA sequences were absent in the mouse genome.
source: To determine if A + T-rich, CpG-rich sequences also exist naturally in mice, we divided the genome into windows of 100 bp and calculated the G + C content and CpG density of each. To ensure that we selected regions with profiles consistently above the thresholds (as is the case for our artificial constructs) rather than short CpG dense regions flanked by AT rich DNA, we subtracted windows with ≥50% GC content or <5 CpGs and searched for blocks of adjoining windows. Uniformly A + T-rich and CpG-rich DNA sequences of this kind were absent in the mouse genome.
evidence: This is a result from computational analysis of the mouse genome.

claim: The high mutation rate of 5-methylcytosine effectively resists CpG accumulation at A + T-rich regions over evolutionary time.
source: As A + T-rich regions are consistently DNA methylated, it seems likely that, in the absence of strong selection, the high mutation rate of 5-methylcytosine effectively resists CpG accumulation at these domains over evolutionary time.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and evolutionary principles.

claim: The non-methylated state of CGIs depends on G + C-rich base composition.
source: We find that the non-methylated state of CGIs depends on G + C-rich base composition and that both the signature histone marks H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 depend on a high density of the non-methylated CpG dyad.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Both the signature histone marks H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 depend on a high density of the non-methylated CpG dyad.
source: We find that the non-methylated state of CGIs depends on G + C-rich base composition and that both the signature histone marks H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 depend on a high density of the non-methylated CpG dyad.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: DNA sequence motifs that are recognised by transcription factors strongly influence DNA methylation patterns.
source: For example, DNA sequence motifs that are recognised by transcription factors strongly influence DNA methylation patterns (Lienert et al., 2011; Stadler et al., 2011) and inter-individual variation in other epigenomic features maps to sites of human DNA sequence heterogeneity that are probably causal (Kasowski et al., 2013; Kilpinen et al., 2013; McVicker et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Almost all native CGIs in mouse ESCs are non-methylated at the DNA level and coincide with peaks of H3K4me3.
source: Almost all native CGIs in mouse ESCs are non-methylated at the DNA level and coincide with peaks of H3K4me3, which is often seen as the signature histone mark of CGIs (Bernstein et al., 2006; Thomson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: About one third of the H3K4me3-marked CGIs in mouse ES cells also carry H3K27me3 and are therefore defined as bivalent.
source: About one third of the H3K4me3-marked CGIs in mouse ES cells also carry H3K27me3 and are therefore defined as bivalent (Ku et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: At least 97% of peaks corresponding to the PRC2 component Ezh2 coincide with CGIs.
source: It is estimated that at least 97% of peaks corresponding to the PRC2 component Ezh2 coincide with CGIs (Ku et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: CpG density within the non-methylated CGI fraction as a whole is proportional to the H3K4me3 ChIP-seq signal in both mouse and human cells.
source: It was shown previously that CpG density within the non-methylated CGI fraction as a whole is proportional to the H3K4me3 ChIP-seq signal in both mouse and human cells (Illingworth et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: 92% of exclusively bivalent promoters from mouse ESCs coincide with CGIs.
source: Within a set of 2547 exclusively bivalent promoters from mouse ESCs (Marks et al., 2012; Denissov et al., 2014), we found that 92% coincide with CGIs.
evidence: This is a result from analysis of published ChIP-seq data.

claim: Within bivalent CGIs, CGI length and CpG density both correlate positively with H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 levels.
source: Within this bivalent group, CGI length and CpG density both correlate positively with H3K4me3 and also H3K27me3 levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in the figure.

claim: Endogenous G + C-rich, CpG-poor sequences do not display a bivalent chromatin structure.
source: In contrast to typical CGI-like sequences, endogenous G + C-rich, CpG-poor sequences do not display a bivalent chromatin structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on genomic analysis.

claim: A + T-rich, CpG-rich domains of CGI-like dimensions are effectively absent from the mouse genome.
source: A + T-rich, CpG-rich domains of CGI-like dimensions, however, are effectively absent from the mouse genome.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on genomic analysis.

claim: A high abundance of the dinucleotide CpG is a key precondition for the formation of bivalent chromatin.
source: The sum of available data argues strongly that a high abundance of the dinucleotide CpG is a key precondition for the formation of bivalent chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion based on all the experimental and genomic data.

claim: In Mll1 and Mll2 the DNA binding domains are within the SET-containing protein themselves.
source: In Mll1 and Mll2 the DNA binding domains are within the SET-containing protein themselves (Allen et al., 2006; Cierpicki et al., 2010), whereas in the case of Set1/COMPASS the CXXC domain resides in the Cfp1 protein component of the multi-subunit complex (Lee and Skalnik, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: In the case of Set1/COMPASS the CXXC domain resides in the Cfp1 protein component of the multi-subunit complex.
source: In Mll1 and Mll2 the DNA binding domains are within the SET-containing protein themselves (Allen et al., 2006; Cierpicki et al., 2010), whereas in the case of Set1/COMPASS the CXXC domain resides in the Cfp1 protein component of the multi-subunit complex (Lee and Skalnik, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The H3K4me3 component of bivalent CGIs in ESCs depends on Mll2.
source: The H3K4me3 component of bivalent CGIs in ESCs depends on Mll2 (Hu et al., 2013; Denissov et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The binding of the CXXC domain to CpG is abolished by methylation of the cytosine moiety.
source: Since the binding of the CXXC domain to CpG is abolished by methylation of the cytosine moiety (Lee et al., 2001), this may explain why DNA methylation prevents the formation of H3K4me3 even in the presence of high CpG densities.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: DNA methylation prevents the formation of H3K4me3 even in the presence of high CpG densities.
source: Since the binding of the CXXC domain to CpG is abolished by methylation of the cytosine moiety (Lee et al., 2001), this may explain why DNA methylation prevents the formation of H3K4me3 even in the presence of high CpG densities.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion based on experimental findings and known molecular mechanisms.

claim: The CXXC-domain protein KDM2B can target the PRC1 complex to CGIs and recruit PRC2 secondarily.
source: A recent study, however, indicates that the CXXC-domain protein KDM2B can target the PRC1 complex to CGIs and recruit PRC2 secondarily, which would accord with our findings (Blackledge et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: H3K27me and H3K4me can be present on the same nucleosome, albeit on different histone tails.
source: Recent evidence has clearly established that H3K27me and H3K4me can be present on the same nucleosome, albeit on different histone tails (Voigt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Silent CGI promoters in ESCs grown in serum usually exhibit a bivalent chromatin structure.
source: Whereas silent CGI promoters in ESCs grown in serum usually exhibit a bivalent chromatin structure, this chromatin configuration is significantly reduced in 2i medium, which discourages differentiation and is thought to induce a more pronounced pluripotent state (Marks et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Bivalent chromatin configuration is significantly reduced in 2i medium.
source: Whereas silent CGI promoters in ESCs grown in serum usually exhibit a bivalent chromatin structure, this chromatin configuration is significantly reduced in 2i medium, which discourages differentiation and is thought to induce a more pronounced pluripotent state (Marks et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Cells in which the histone methyltransferase Mll2 is depleted lose H3K4me3 at hitherto bivalent CGIs, but this has no detectable effect on the induction kinetics of the associated genes upon differentiation.
source: Also, cells in which the histone methyltransferase Mll2 is depleted lose H3K4me3 at hitherto bivalent CGIs, but this has no detectable effect on the induction kinetics of the associated genes upon differentiation (Hu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Bivalency is not confined to poised developmental genes but is a default response to any CpG-rich DNA sequences, even when these are completely artificial.
source: Here we find that bivalency is not confined to poised developmental genes but is a default response to any CpG-rich DNA sequences, even when these are completely artificial.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the experimental findings with artificial CGIs.

claim: The bivalent chromatin structure is not reserved for developmentally important genes, but is a response to general features of local DNA sequence.
source: It is apparent from this that the bivalent chromatin structure is not reserved for developmentally important genes, but is a response to general features of local DNA sequence.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Bulk mammalian DNA has a base composition of 40% G + C and is globally methylated at CpGs to an average level of ∼65%.
source: Bulk mammalian DNA has a base composition of 40% G + C and is globally methylated at CpGs to an average level of ∼65%, whereas G + C-rich CGIs are usually DNA methylation-free.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as established knowledge.

claim: G + C-rich CGI-like DNA reproducibly resisted DNA methylation, whereas A + T-rich DNA reliably became densely methylated.
source: The transfection experiments reported here recapitulate this distinction as G + C-rich CGI-like DNA reproducibly resisted DNA methylation, whereas A + T-rich DNA reliably became densely methylated.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings stated in the Discussion.

claim: The broadly binary pattern of global DNA methylation may be determined by base composition.
source: Our findings raise the possibility that this broadly binary pattern of global DNA methylation may be determined by base composition.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the Discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: CpG density did not affect susceptibility to methylation, which occurred even when CpG occurred at densities typical of endogenous CGIs.
source: CpG density did not affect this susceptibility to methylation, which occurred even when CpG occurred at densities typical of endogenous CGIs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on experimental findings with A+T-rich, CpG-rich constructs.

claim: Both Dnmt 3L and Dnmt 3A have the potential to be repelled by H3K4me3.
source: Both Dnmt 3L and Dnmt 3A have the potential to be repelled by H3K4me3 (Jia et al., 2007; Ooi et al., 2007), suggesting that recruitment of H3K4 methyltransferases with CpG-binding CXXC domains protects CGIs against de novo methylation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Recruitment of H3K4 methyltransferases with CpG-binding CXXC domains protects CGIs against de novo methylation.
source: Both Dnmt 3L and Dnmt 3A have the potential to be repelled by H3K4me3 (Jia et al., 2007; Ooi et al., 2007), suggesting that recruitment of H3K4 methyltransferases with CpG-binding CXXC domains protects CGIs against de novo methylation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the Discussion based on cited literature.

claim: A + T-rich CpG-rich sequences are reproducibly DNA methylated despite their ability to attract H3K4me3 when DNA methylation is absent.
source: We find, however, that A + T-rich CpG-rich sequences are reproducibly DNA methylated despite their ability to attract H3K4me3 when DNA methylation is absent.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on experimental findings.

claim: H3K4me3 alone is not sufficient to exclude CpG methylation from A + T-rich, CpG-rich regions.
source: Since these sequences were initially non-methylated when transfected into cells, it may be that H3K4me3 alone is not sufficient to exclude CpG methylation from these regions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the Discussion based on experimental observations.

claim: A moderately G + C-rich artificial CGI when inserted into ES cells was extensively methylated despite the presence of H3K4me3 on non-methylated copies.
source: This would accord with our previous observation that a moderately G + C-rich artificial CGI when inserted into ES cells was extensively methylated despite the presence of H3K4me3 on non-methylated copies (Thomson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The CGI phenomenon is conserved throughout the vertebrate lineage.
source: The CGI phenomenon is conserved throughout the vertebrate lineage, but interestingly the G + C-richness characteristic of mammalian and bird CGIs is not seen in some vertebrate groups (Long et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The G + C-richness characteristic of mammalian and bird CGIs is not seen in some vertebrate groups.
source: The CGI phenomenon is conserved throughout the vertebrate lineage, but interestingly the G + C-richness characteristic of mammalian and bird CGIs is not seen in some vertebrate groups (Long et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Fish have non-methylated CGI-like sequences at promoters, but these are not markedly G + C-rich compared with the bulk genome.
source: Fish for example have non-methylated CGI-like sequences at promoters, but these are not markedly G + C-rich compared with the bulk genome (Cross et al., 1991; Long et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Some vertebrate groups may rely on a different set of mechanisms to prevent methylation at G + C-poor CGIs.
source: Since A + T-rich sequences are susceptible to de novo DNA methylation in mammals, it follows that some vertebrate groups may rely on a different set of mechanisms to prevent methylation at G + C-poor CGIs.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion based on the experimental findings and comparative biology.
